verdict: Accepted. No source review objection; actual native fade-free capture acceptance remains pending.
scope: Read-only review and independent focused execution of readiness-aware native image fade suppression; no source edits, native/CI rerun or test weakening.
sourceFindings: Installed React Native 0.81.5 ReactImageView.kt:423–427 uses explicit fadeDurationMs when nonnegative, 0 for resource images, otherwise REMOTE_IMAGE_FADE_DURATION_MS=300 at 616. The JS fadeDuration prop reaches setFadeDuration via ReactImageManager.kt:216–218.

ReactImageView reports load/loadEnd from onFinalImageSet, independently of the hierarchy fade duration. The existing capture pipeline waits for decode/readiness and two animation frames; that does not explicitly wait for the native hierarchy fade to complete.

StoryPixelImage sets fadeDuration=0 only when its existing StoryPhotoReadinessContext reporter is present. Otherwise its prop remains undefined. Source/fit/key/style and load/error callbacks are unchanged.

That context is active in both the visible StoryComposer canvas/export artwork and the MemoryMovieExport preview/capture tree. The scope is readiness-aware capture surfaces, not solely an offscreen renderer. Ordinary viewer/feed playback without the context retains the native default.

The graded-photo branch still selects GradedPhoto and its existing Skia decode/layout/readiness path. Photo stickers explicitly opt out of the inherited image grade and now receive the same nonfading native Image prop during capture.
No delay, timeout, retry, encoded-media verifier tolerance, capability flag, source permission or cancellation behavior was changed.

retainedImageReview.visualInspection: The retained photo has darkened four quadrants; the sticker is dark green while its white frame remains opaque. Both PNGs were opened and inspected.
retainedImageReview.interpretation: The common-alpha fit and installed image fade source strongly support a capture taken during presentation fade. They do not prove a later native run is corrected.

limits: The component harness executes actual production TSX with controlled React hooks/native Image/Skia hosts. It verifies props and callback routing, not an Android image animation or new on-device capture.
Existing pixel cases exercise real color-matrix calculations; the new graded-path case verifies branch selection and callback preservation, not a new Skia GPU screenshot.
The numerical projection uses four interior quadrant samples and the known fixture background. It is a source-over fit, not a measurement of the native animation clock.
Full native capture/encode/decode/save/cleanup acceptance remains mandatory.
